paragraphs: First check whether the target is a postmaster or mail superintendent: the main deliverables are safe, traceable postal operations, staff scheduling, handling customer problems and reporting to superiors, not personally completing all frontline transactions.

Observable signals: can trace incoming items, outgoing items, shifts and complaint data back to their source, and distinguish exceptions, authorized decisions and the next responsible person; can explain how scheduling choices affect staff and mail service.

Safe trial: using the fictional shift A mail backlog, shift B staffing shortfall and item C complaint, write one page of shift and handling decisions; do not use real users, staff, mail or institutional systems.

Self-check: first check mail volumes and shift coverage; staffing shortfalls must not be covered by falsifying attendance, backlogs must not be falsely recorded as handled, and complaints must record the facts and follow-up responsibility. Budgets, staffing and service commitments are made only within authorized scope.

Those who prefer organizing people and postal service quality and are willing to verify records and handle conflicts can continue looking at specific superintendent announcements; if they prefer individual acceptance, sorting or delivery, compare the corresponding detailed occupations.

This page discusses only O*NET 11-9131 Postmasters and Mail Superintendents, which refers to organizing, directing or coordinating operations, administrative, managerial and support services at US post offices. BLS gives it a separate occupation line; Chinese postal institution job titles and authority are not automatically mutually recognized.

Core tasks include checking attendance and scheduling, organizing incoming and outgoing mail processing, resolving customer complaints, training and evaluating staff, and submitting operations reports to superiors. Procurement and office facilities may be supplementary tasks in some positions and should not outweigh the main line of mail flow, service and staff supervision.

entries: Mail operations｜organize incoming and outgoing items and station handover｜verify real quantities, status and exceptions, and do not write plans as completed.
Staff scheduling｜prepare shifts and check attendance and work coverage｜staffing shortfalls and overtime are handled under institutional procedures, without falsifying records.
Customer issues｜investigate complaints and service discrepancies｜verify item numbers, receipts and handling responsibility, and protect user information.
Training and evaluation｜coach staff and record work performance｜equipment, charging and route authority are granted by the institution.
Operations reporting｜summarize mail volumes, service problems and resource needs｜data sources, timing and definitions can be reviewed.
Management boundaries｜handling labour disputes and resource matters requires compliant authorization｜legal powers or budget authority cannot be inferred from the job title.

items.title: What occupational characteristics and preparation conditions need to be checked before recruitment?

values: Materials and timing｜45 minutes, entirely fictional

5 minutes to read the task, 15 minutes to write the three-event operations sheet, 10 minutes for handover, 10 minutes to score and correct errors, 5 minutes to review. Shift A: the system received 120 items and shows 100 handled, with the whereabouts of the remaining 20 pending verification; the system count is not the physical fact. Shift B: 4 people were scheduled and 3 reported, with no hours or approvable shift adjustment given. Item C: the customer says it was not received, and the task provides no verifiable proof of delivery.

All quantities, names, item numbers, sites and times are fictional; the handover time is T0, with the processing lead checking A, the scheduling lead checking B and the customer service lead checking C. There is no need to touch real mail, attendance, systems or personal data.
Deliverables and fields

Write the operations sheet in three columns A/B/C, keeping the original source, known facts, unknowns, current status, proposed verification actions, next responsible person and the T0 review arrangement separate in each column. Proposed actions must not be written as completed.

The handover note states clearly the 20-item discrepancy, the 1-person staffing gap and the unverified C complaint; it states separately the records or authorizations still to be checked, and does not fabricate approvals, compensation promises or confirmed delivery.
Complete reference answer

A: the system received 120 and shows 100 handled, a difference of 20; the whereabouts of the 20 are unknown, and the reality of the 100 also awaits physical and record verification, so 120 cannot be falsely recorded as complete. T0 is referred to the processing lead to check scans, batches and site status, and the status is corrected only after clarification.

B: 4 scheduled, 3 reported, a gap of 1; the 4th person's attendance must not be falsified. The task cannot determine that the shift is covered or directly approve a shift adjustment; T0 is referred to the scheduling lead to check hours, coverage and approval under the rules. C: there is only the customer's statement of non-receipt and no proof of delivery; keep it unverified, do not assert delivery or promise compensation, and refer T0 to the customer service lead to check the item number and records and follow up under approved procedures.

The handover review gives 120−100=20 and 4−3=1, but the differences are not physical backlog or confirmed vacancy hours; another person should be able to distinguish system, site and customer statements and find the three T0 responsible persons.
Scoring, error samples and feedback

Four dimensions scored 0–2 each, 8 in total: mail verification, staff coverage facts, complaint evidence and handover, and data and authority. 2 points means the facts, unknowns, actions and responsible persons are complete and correct; 1 point means the direction is right but verification or handover fields are missing; 0 points means falsified status or attendance, asserting delivery without evidence, inability to hand over, or use of real data or exceeding authority.

The error sample is entirely fictional and does not exceed authority, but writes A120 items as complete, the 4th shift B person as present and C as delivered with no T0 responsible person: 0/0/0/2=2/8. Feedback: restore A's system 100 with the 20 unknown, B's 1-person gap and C unverified, and add the three T0 responsible persons and the records to be checked. The score is learning feedback only, not a recruitment examination. Real personnel, mail, compensation and equipment decisions follow institutional training and authorization.

subject.name: Postmasters and Mail Superintendents
subject.summary: Postmasters and mail superintendents correspond to US O*NET 11-9131: they organize and supervise postal acceptance, processing, delivery and support work, arrange shifts, check attendance, handle customer complaints, train staff and report operations to superiors. It is a postal operations management position, not the Office Manager occupation or a wage substitute for frontline counter, sorting or delivery positions. Actual appointment, charging, equipment, staffing and information authority follow institutional rules.
